summary: A 1821 light on a small island at Boothbay Harbor's western entrance: an 1888 fix for the Cuckolds, a keeper's log, a state living museum today.

notes_for_editor: Conflicts left open in the story: (1) Masonry: LighthouseFriends granite lined with brick; NRHP fieldstone, brick and cement; USLHS rubble stone. (2) Dwelling: NRHP gives the wood-frame dwelling as built 1821; LighthouseFriends and USLHS date the present house to 1857 and say it replaced a stone cottage. (3) Characteristic dates: NRHP about 1890 for fixed red and 1892 for flashing red; LighthouseFriends 1889 and 1901 (square lens). The NRHP's 1909 description gives flashing every five seconds, which matches LighthouseFriends. The record's 'Fl R 6s' was not checked against a Light List and is not used. (4) Lens locations: LighthouseFriends places the fourth-order lens at the Maine Lighthouse Museum and the 1961 square lens at the Maine Maritime Museum; both are used as printed. (5) The McCobb log entries are quoted as LighthouseFriends prints them from the National Archives originals, which were not read directly. (6) The 1875 schooner James Somes wreck: a Chronicling America search for the name in Maine papers, 1875-1876, found no hits; the story uses the log alone and says so. (7) The Lighthouse Board reports for 1880s and 1890s are in the corpus only from 1891; the 1888 dead angle and the 1889-1892 characteristic changes are not checked against a Board report. (8) Living persons: Henry Sieg and the Muise family are named by role and the published interpretation only; no personal details beyond what LighthouseFriends prints. (9) NRHP listing date not confirmed from the NPGallery page (no date shown); the story says only that the station is on the Register. (10) Wikipedia was read for leads only (it gives automation in 1989; USLHS and LighthouseFriends give 1988) and is not cited. (11) Access: LighthouseFriends says grounds, dwelling and tower open; the boat-only point is inferred from its visitor information (tours land on the island), not stated as such. Fact-check 2026-10-22: 'western entrance' is supported by the NRHP text ('built in 1821 on the west side of the entrance to Boothbay Harbor') and is now footnoted to it. The sentence on the 1875 wreck no longer says the sources read; it says no other account is cited. Footnote gaps were closed on the harbour purpose, the dwelling date and the boat access. Burnt Island's FY1895 bell tower (scan page 227) sits in a volume whose opening pages are dated June 30, 1895, so the fiscal year is 1895; the FY1896 bell entry (scan page 52) lies inside the report whose header is at scan page 11 (the next header is at scan page 245). The 1899 oil house (scan page 80) is in the report dated 1899. Quotations from McCobb's log and the 1837 Navy report are public-domain primary text printed by LighthouseFriends and footnoted to that page. Fact-check 2026-10-22 (late edit): the log entry says only that the wife died in March 1877; the story no longer says where.
